title: The Measure Problem
description: In a universe that lasts forever, everything that can fluctuate into being does, infinitely often - even a lone brain that only thinks it remembers a world. How then to say what is likely? Unlocks the deliberate assembly of a Boltzmann Brain.

puzzle.goal: Fluctuations out of equilibrium are rarer the more entropy they cost. Write how many times likelier Q a fluctuation that costs s of entropy is than one costing S, with Boltzmann's k.
puzzle.name: Einstein's inversion
puzzle.ask: Find Q for S = @{S}, s = @{s} and k = @{k} (entropies in units of k).

vars.S: entropy cost of the larger fluctuation

puzzle.method: Einstein: a fluctuation that lowers the entropy by ΔS has probability ∝ e^(−ΔS/k). A brain is far cheaper than a universe.
